item.title: How to build agents that survive crashes with Pi Durable
item.content:encoded: Build a durable TypeScript agent with Pi Durable and SQLite. Test crash recovery, avoid duplicate requests, and understand which tools can safely run again.

item.title: A deep dive into OpenSEO
item.content:encoded: Explore OpenSEO's architecture: SEO data APIs, Cloudflare Workers, its audit crawler, MCP tools, AI agents, storage, and self-hosting trade-offs.

item.title: How to write an OpenCode plugin with the v2 API
item.content:encoded: Build your first OpenCode v2 plugin in TypeScript, register a custom tool, validate its inputs, test the logic, and understand how v1 plugins change.

item.title: Build vs buy software: when AI can replace a SaaS
item.content:encoded: AI changes the build-versus-buy calculation, but a working prototype is only part of it. How to compare ownership, maintenance, risk, and recurring costs.

item.title: How to compete with AI-generated SaaS clones
item.content:encoded: Cheap software clones change what a small SaaS business can charge for. A practical look at differentiation, maintenance, distribution, and earning trust.

item.title: Meta released Muse Spark Open: what you can run, and what it takes
item.content:encoded: Meta released Muse Spark Open with downloadable weights, a million-token context, and support for coding agents. Here are the hardware and license limits.

item.title: The complete guide to Void: full-stack Vite apps with Hono and Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: Build and deploy full-stack Vite apps with Void, Hono, React, and Cloudflare D1. Learn typed routes, forms, migrations, authentication, and team hosting.

item.title: How to use OpenCode
item.content:encoded: Learn how to install OpenCode, connect a model, make your first code change, and configure project instructions and permissions in this hands-on tutorial.

item.title: What “open weights” means for AI models
item.content:encoded: Learn what open weights means for AI models, how it differs from open source, and what the Qwen3.8 and Kimi K3 downloads show about licenses and scale.

item.title: How to handle web requests in C with CGI 1.1
item.content:encoded: Learn CGI 1.1 by building a C web application: read requests, decode forms, return HTML and errors, and run the executable through Apache.

item.title: A deep dive into LangChain and LangGraph
item.content:encoded: Learn LangChain and LangGraph with TypeScript: models, prompts, tools, agents, memory, streaming, RAG, graphs, persistence, and human approval.

item.title: How I fixed a full Ubuntu server disk with Codex
item.content:encoded: My Sendy server stopped responding with the disk at 99%. The database was 528 MB, but MySQL binary logs had grown to 41 GB. Here is how Codex walked me through finding them, purging them safely, and setting an expiry so it never happens again.

item.title: How to create an Apple TV app
item.content:encoded: Build a tvOS app with SwiftUI, share code with your Mac app, design it for the Siri Remote, make its layered icon, and install it on your own Apple TV.

item.title: How to install your own apps on your iPhone with Xcode
item.content:encoded: Put the apps you build on your iPhone without the App Store: turn on Developer Mode, install from Xcode, update over Wi-Fi from the terminal, and renew them.

item.title: How to use Jev with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
item.content:encoded: How to use Jev with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor: install TypeSafe's agent skill, give the agent the docs, and review the Jev code it writes.

item.title: The complete guide to LiveKit Agents
item.content:encoded: Build a voice AI agent with LiveKit Agents in Node.js and TypeScript, then test it, simulate calls, deploy it to LiveKit Cloud and watch real sessions.

item.title: How to compile JavaScript into a single executable
item.content:encoded: Turn a JavaScript program into one executable file, like Go and Rust do, with deno compile, bun build --compile and Node.js single executable apps.

item.title: Use WhatCable to figure out what your USB cable can do
item.content:encoded: WhatCable is a free, open source Mac app that reads the chip inside a USB-C cable and tells you its real data speed, power rating and what limits it.

item.title: How to avoid the "Open Anyway" message when building macOS apps
item.content:encoded: macOS blocks apps downloaded from the internet until people click Open Anyway. Sign your app with a Developer ID and notarize it, and it opens normally.

item.title: What happens when AI agents shop for us
item.content:encoded: Shopify wants Muse to check out with Shop Pay on every store. I want the agent to find the product. I still want a person to approve the exact charge.

item.title: Use npkill to find and delete old node_modules folders
item.content:encoded: npkill is a free terminal tool that finds every node_modules folder on your computer, shows its size and age, and deletes the ones you pick.

item.title: I built Repo Foyer, a Chrome extension that puts my repos on the GitHub home page
item.content:encoded: Repo Foyer is my free, open source Chrome extension that replaces the GitHub home page with your repositories, so you can jump to the one you're working on.

item.title: I open sourced testvm, so your coding agents can test Mac apps in a VM
item.content:encoded: testvm is my free, open source tool that runs Mac app builds in a headless macOS VM, so coding agents test them without taking over your screen.

item.title: I built Footage Ferry, a Mac app to import Blackmagic Camera videos
item.content:encoded: Footage Ferry is my free, open source Mac app that copies Blackmagic Camera clips from an iPhone over USB, checks every copy byte for byte, and then offers to delete the originals.

item.title: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK
item.content:encoded: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK: install the TypeSafe provider, call experimental_evaluate, read confidence, use AI Gateway, and compare Jev with an LLM.

item.title: I built Chip Pops, 6,000 8-bit sound effects for my apps
item.content:encoded: Chip Pops is my free, open source Mac app and command line tool with about 6,000 8-bit sound effects made with jsfxr. Click a sound to hear it, drag it into your app.

item.title: I built Couch Snake, the classic phone game for the Apple TV
item.content:encoded: Couch Snake is my free, open source Apple TV game: the classic snake game from old mobile phones, full screen on a green LCD board, steered by swiping on the Siri Remote.

item.title: How to use cf, the new Cloudflare CLI
item.content:encoded: Learn cf, the new Cloudflare CLI: find commands with cf cli search, configure Workers in cloudflare.config.ts, deploy, and migrate from Wrangler.

item.content:encoded: Answer four questions and get three hosts that fit your project, with a monthly price and the main catch. 21 providers, prices checked October 1, 2026.

item.content:encoded: Find a payment provider for your product, compare fees on your own numbers, and see who handles tax and disputes. Merchant of Record and direct providers.
